chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is not upon the women to be loud with the Talbiyya, nor to touch the Stone, nor to enter the House, nor to perform Sa'y between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, meaning the Harwala (trotting).

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: The loud recitation of 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk' during Hajj
key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa, one of the two hills in Mecca
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa, the second hill in Mecca
key_terms.الْهَرْوَلَةَ: The trotting or hurrying walk performed by men during Sa'y

ai.seo_question: What are the exemptions for women regarding Hajj rituals like Talbiyya and Sa'y?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical accommodations granted to women during Hajj, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (yusr) and the distinction between obligatory acts (wajib) and recommended ones (mustahabb) based on gender. It specifically exempts women from the vigorous trotting (harwala) during Sa'y and the loud recitation of Talbiyya, aligning with the principle that these acts are not strictly binding upon them. This ruling underscores the flexibility in ritual performance to accommodate women's physical circumstances without compromising the validity of their pilgrimage.
